import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1121

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1121](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1121)
- [BeLi16] Bezdek, Károly and Litvak, Alexander E., *Packing convex bodies by cylinders*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. (2016), 725-738.
- [GoGo45] Goodman, A. W. and Goodman, R. E., *A circle covering theorem*. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (1945), 494-498.
- [Ha47] Hadwiger, H., *Nonseparable convex systems*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 583-585.
-/

namespace Erdos1121

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/--
If $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ are circles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no line
disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets then the circles can be
covered by a circle of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

This is true, and was proved by Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] (whose proof also generalises to
higher dimensions). A generalisation to convex bodies was proved by Hadwiger [Ha47].

An alternative proof is given by Bezdek and Litvak [BeLi16].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1121.lean"]
theorem erdos_1121 {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ²) (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : ℝ²) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : ℝ², (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

/--
The proof of Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] also generalises to higher dimensions: if
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no hyperplane
disjoint from all the balls divides them into two non-empty sets then the balls can be covered by
a ball of radius $r=\sum r_i$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1121

reformulations.difference: The source prohibits a disjoint line separating the disks into two nonempty groups. Lean represents lines by nonzero normals and offsets, and requires all centers to lie strictly on the same side whenever the line misses every closed ball.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every planar line has the form {p | inner ℝ v p = t} with v ≠ 0. A closed ball of positive radius contains its center and is convex. If the line misses the ball, continuity of the inner product and the intermediate value theorem imply that every point of that ball lies on the center's side. Since no center lies on the line, absence of balls on opposite sides is equivalent to the stated disjunction of universal inequalities. The equivalence with absence of a separating normal-form hyperplane was proved in scratch.lean as Review1121.centerCondition_iff_no_separating, without sorry-backed dependencies.

reformulations.difference: The higher-dimensional statement likewise expresses nonseparability through normal vectors and the positions of centers rather than through partitions of whole balls by hyperplanes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space every proper affine hyperplane admits the stated nonzero-normal representation. The same convexity and intermediate-value argument identifies the side of each ball with the side of its center. The scratch equivalence is proved for arbitrary real inner-product spaces, so it applies in every dimension here. Dimension zero introduces no exception: there are no nonzero normals, and the covering conclusion holds because the ambient space is a singleton.

review.notes: Both declarations are faithful. Bezdek–Litvak explicitly use closed circular disks, and Goodman–Goodman explicitly state that their proof generalizes to Euclidean k-space. Lean tests passed for n = 0, n = 1, d = 0, tangent disks, separated disks, and the Euclidean metric. The cited formal proof was checked after one tactic-only compatibility change (convert to convert!) from its older Mathlib version; a bridge to the exact current planar statement compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
